% glossaries' main glossary, acronyms, symbols, numbers, a glossary from
% \newglossary* (output .notation-gls), and one from \newglossary with its
% own extensions (output .tls), each with its sorted file beside the
% document from an earlier build: an entry whose number is in \hyperpage,
% which the document no longer defines
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[acronym,symbols,numbers]{glossaries}
\newglossary*{notation}{Notation}
\newglossary[tlg]{terms}{tls}{tlo}{Terms}
\makeglossaries
\newglossaryentry{fruit}{name={fruit},description={the seed-bearing part of a plant}}
\newacronym{tla}{TLA}{three-letter acronym}
\newglossaryentry{pi}{type=symbols,name={pi},sort={pi},description={a circle's circumference over its diameter}}
\newglossaryentry{seven}{type=numbers,name={seven},description={the number of days in a week}}
\newglossaryentry{hom}{type=notation,name={Hom},description={the set of homomorphisms}}
\newglossaryentry{ring}{type=terms,name={ring},description={a set with two operations}}
\begin{document}
A \gls{fruit}, a \gls{tla}, \gls{pi}, \gls{seven}, \gls{hom}, and a \gls{ring}.
\printglossary
\printglossary[type=\acronymtype]
\printglossary[type=symbols]
\printglossary[type=numbers]
\printglossary[type=notation]
\printglossary[type=terms]
\end{document}
